blocks.md: **US imports from China grew more than twelvefold between 1991/92 and 2007, from \$26 billion to \$330 billion (2007 dollars), far faster than US exports to China or imports from anywhere else. Eight other high-income countries saw almost the same surge.**

blocks.src: assets/Attachments/US imports from China and manufacturing employment 1987-2007.png
blocks.alt: US imports from China and manufacturing employment 1987-2007

blocks.md: China's import penetration ratio rose from ≈0.002 (1987) to ≈0.047 (2007), while the share of the US working-age population employed in manufacturing fell from ≈0.135 to ≈0.083 (read off the chart).

blocks.src: assets/Attachments/Table - Trade with China, US and other high-income countries 1991-2007.png
blocks.alt: Table - Trade with China, US and other high-income countries 1991-2007

blocks.md:
- **Imports, not trade overall**: the US trade relationship with China became very unbalanced — imports grew far faster than exports.
- **Common across rich countries**: other developed countries' imports from China grew almost as fast. That common component is what the [Shift-Share Instrument](note:shift-share-instrument) exploits — it reflects China's own growth rather than US demand.
- Exports to China are reported from 1992, the first year available.
